// pathFilters: Until this file existed, CS2OpenDev.Sdk.GameEvents inherited the root
version.json, whose pathFilters are `:/src/CS2OpenDev.Sdk/` — which does
not prefix-match `src/CS2OpenDev.Sdk.GameEvents/`. A commit touching only
this project therefore produced no version change, so a GameEvents-only
fix could be built, tagged and pushed and the feed would reject it as a
duplicate. It only ever moved when a schema regen happened to touch the
Generated/ lives under this directory, so a regen that changes the event
records is caught here without naming the generator or the schema.
// versionHeightOffset: Cancels the commit that changes `version` above, so a MAJOR.MINOR bump cuts a
real X.Y.0 instead of X.Y.1.
Nerdbank.GitVersioning counts height from the commit that last changed
`version`, and that commit is itself height 1 -- so the first release of every
new MAJOR.MINOR landed as .1 and no .0 has ever existed here. 22 released
versions, zero ending in .0. Shipping `5.0.1` as the first 5.0 implies a 5.0.0
that was superseded, which never existed.
This MUST be introduced alongside a MAJOR.MINOR bump. Adding it mid-stream
shifts the next resolved version DOWN by one, which can land below what is
already on the feed -- exactly the trap CS2OpenDev.Sdk.GameEvents' positive
offset was created to escape, in the other direction.
Cannot make height negative in practice: the offset only applies from the
commit that sets it, which is a `version` change, so height is at least 1.
Gone, and deliberately. It existed for one job: this package switched to
its own clock while 2.0.4 was already published, and a restarted height
would have produced a version BELOW the one on the feed, leaving NuGet
serving 2.0.4 as newest forever. The offset bought clearance.
The 3.0 bump does that job on its own — any 3.0.x outranks every 2.0.x —
so keeping the offset would only inflate the patch number for no reason.
Restore it if this package ever switches clocks again inside a major.
